proposals.headline: Azure demand evidence strengthened
proposals.whatChanged: Azure grew 39% year over year versus the demo team's 34.5% constant-currency base case, while Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $46.7 billion.
proposals.againstOurView: The approved demo thesis expected durable mid-30s Azure growth but held only medium conviction before results.
proposals.whyItMatters: The reported acceleration strengthens the demand pillar, although reported and constant-currency bases should not be treated as identical.
uncertainties: Azure reported growth and the pre-event constant-currency forecast use different bases.
Capacity constraints may still defer some demand conversion.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Reconcile reported and constant-currency Azure growth and track capacity delivery through FY2026 H1.

proposals.headline: Capacity constraint duration increased
proposals.whatChanged: Management expected Azure to remain capacity constrained through the first half of FY2026 despite continued datacenter additions.
proposals.againstOurView: The approved demo thesis expected capacity additions to prevent a prolonged constraint after FY2025 Q4.
proposals.whyItMatters: A longer constraint raises execution and timing risk for backlog conversion and makes quarterly Azure growth more dependent on capacity delivery.
uncertainties: Management did not quantify revenue deferred by the constraint.
The delivery schedule and workload mix can change quarter to quarter.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Track capacity commissioning, finance-lease timing, and Azure growth sensitivity through FY2026 H1.

proposals.headline: Cloud margin forecast requires review
proposals.whatChanged: Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 68%, one point above the demo team's 67% base case, while quarterly capital expenditures reached $24.2 billion.
proposals.againstOurView: The approved forecast expected 67% cloud gross margin and assumed efficiency gains would offset part of AI infrastructure pressure.
proposals.whyItMatters: The quarter was modestly better than the base case, but the scale and mix of capital spending remain central to long-term AI economics.
uncertainties: Gross margin alone does not measure the return on incremental AI capital.
Finance leases create quarter-to-quarter capex timing variability.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Review the cloud margin bridge and separate long-lived datacenter assets from shorter-lived compute equipment.

proposals.headline: Test growth against rising AI capital intensity
proposals.whatChanged: FY2026 Q1 Azure growth was guided to approximately 37% constant currency while cloud gross margin was expected near 67% and capacity remained constrained.
proposals.againstOurView: The demo team forecast assumed 35% Azure growth but did not define an explicit test connecting growth, margin, and incremental capital requirements.
proposals.whyItMatters: A governed thesis needs a measurable way to distinguish productive capacity investment from growth that consumes progressively more capital.
uncertainties: The company does not disclose Azure revenue or workload-level return on invested capital.
Capital expenditure timing includes finance-lease variability.
proposals.recommendedFollowUp: Track Azure growth, cloud gross margin, capex mix, and management commentary as one evidence cluster.

value.question: Is accelerating Azure growth producing adequate returns relative to the rising level and mix of AI capital expenditure?
